title: Data Ontology: Definition, Examples, and Palantir's Model
summary: Data ontology, explained with one example built four ways: taxonomy, ontology, knowledge graph, semantic layer. Plus how Palantir's Ontology works.
body_markdown:
Ask three data platforms what an ontology is and you’ll get three answers. Palantir says its Ontology is[“not a ‘semantic layer’.”](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/architecture-center/ontology-system/) Microsoft says its new ontology[“provides a common context layer.”](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/ontology/overview) Databricks calls it[“the context layer your AI agents are missing.”](https://www.databricks.com/blog/data-ontology-defined-context-layer-your-ai-agents-are-missing)


They’re all describing the same underlying idea, a data ontology, from different angles. This guide defines it plainly, then shows one business example built four ways (as a taxonomy, an ontology, a knowledge graph, and a semantic layer) so the differences are visible rather than abstract. It also covers how Palantir’s Ontology actually works and what an AI agent really needs.


## Key Takeaways


-


**A data ontology models meaning, not storage:** It defines the things your business cares about, their properties, how they relate, and the rules that apply, independent of how tables are laid out.


-


**Ontology + data = knowledge graph:** The ontology is the blueprint. The knowledge graph is the blueprint filled in with real instances.


-


**Ontologies measurably help AI:** In[data.world’s benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07509) , GPT-4 answered 16.7% of enterprise questions correctly over SQL and 54.2% over a knowledge graph built on an ontology. On the most complex schemas, accuracy went from 0% to over 35%.


-


**There are two kinds of ontology in circulation:** Formal ontologies (OWL, RDF) are built for reasoning. Operational ontologies (Palantir, Microsoft Fabric IQ, Databricks Genie) bind business objects to live data, permissions, and actions.


## What Is a Data Ontology?


A data ontology is a formal, shared model of the things a business cares about (entities such as customers, contracts, and invoices), their attributes, how they relate to each other, and the rules that constrain them. It describes what data means, independently of how it’s stored, so people and machines interpret it the same way.


In simple terms, a data ontology is the agreed-upon answer to “what is a customer here, and how does it connect to everything else?”


### Where the Word Comes From


“Ontology” comes from philosophy, where it means the study of what exists. Computer science borrowed it in the 1990s. Tom Gruber’s widely cited definition calls an ontology[a specification of a conceptualization](https://tomgruber.org/writing/ontolingua-kaj-1993.htm) : an explicit description of the concepts in a domain and the relationships between them. The W3C later standardized the idea as the[Web Ontology Language (OWL)](https://www.w3.org/OWL/) , which is “designed to represent rich and complex knowledge about things, groups of things, and relations between things.”


### Ontology vs Data Model


A data model describes **storage** : tables, columns, data types, and foreign keys. An ontology describes **meaning** : a Customer *holds* Subscriptions, an Invoice *is billed to* exactly one Customer, and an Active Customer is one with at least one live subscription. As Databricks puts it, “A schema describes how data is structured. An ontology describes what that data means in the context of the business.”


You can change the data model (split a table, rename a column) without changing the ontology. That separation is what makes an ontology durable. A[semantic model](https://upsolve.ai/blog/semantic-model) sits between the two: business meaning, scoped to analytics.

## One Example, Four Ways: Taxonomy, Ontology, Knowledge Graph, Semantic Layer


The clearest way to understand these terms is to model the same business domain in each. We’ll use a subscription business with three concepts: **Customer** , **Subscription** , and **Invoice** .


Data ontology vs taxonomy vs knowledge graph vs semantic layer: one subscription-business example modeled four ways


### As a Taxonomy


A taxonomy only says what kind of thing something is. It’s a hierarchy of “is-a” relationships, usually expressed in[SKOS](https://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/) , the W3C standard for taxonomies and thesauri:


-


Customer → Enterprise Customer, SMB Customer


-


Subscription → Monthly Subscription, Annual Subscription


-


Invoice → Open Invoice, Paid Invoice, Overdue Invoice


A taxonomy can’t tell you that a subscription belongs to a customer. There are no relationships across branches.


### As an Ontology


An ontology adds typed relationships, properties, and rules. Here’s a minimal version in Turtle (RDF syntax), with illustrative names:


```text
@prefix :      <https://example.com/billing#>   .
@prefix owl:   <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>   .
@prefix rdfs:  <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>


```

```

@prefix owl:   <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>   .

```


```text
@prefix :      <https://example.com/billing#>   .
@prefix owl:   <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>   .
@prefix rdfs:  <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>


```


On top of that structure, the ontology states rules in business terms. An **Active Customer** is a Customer with at least one Subscription whose status is active or past due. An **Overdue Invoice** is an open Invoice past its due date. There’s still no data here, just the shape of meaning.

A knowledge graph is the ontology populated with real instances.[Enterprise Knowledge’s](https://enterprise-knowledge.com/whats-the-difference-between-an-ontology-and-a-knowledge-graph/) shorthand is that ontology + data = knowledge graph. With fictional data:

Because the rules travel with the graph, a reasoner can infer that INV-8873 is an Overdue Invoice once its due date passes, and that Acme Corp is an Active Customer. That makes multi-hop questions natural: “Which active enterprise customers on the Pro plan have overdue invoices?”


### As a Semantic Layer


A semantic layer takes the same concepts and makes them computable. It maps them to warehouse tables (` dim_customers` ,` fct_subscriptions` ,` fct_invoices` ), declares the joins, and defines metrics that compile to SQL:


-


**ARR** =` SUM(fct_subscriptions.mrr) * 12` where` status IN ('active', 'past_due')`


-


**Overdue AR** =` SUM(fct_invoices.amount)` where` status = 'open' AND due_date < CURRENT_DATE`


-


**Dimensions:** customer segment, region, plan


A semantic layer is less expressive than an ontology. It can’t reason about classes. But it’s deterministic: ARR computes the same way every time, in every tool. The dbt Semantic Layer and[the Cube semantic layer](https://upsolve.ai/blog/cube-semantic-layer) work this way; our[semantic layer tools comparison](https://upsolve.ai/blog/semantic-layer-tools) covers the rest.

## Ontology vs Knowledge Graph


A knowledge graph is not the same as an ontology. The ontology is the schema. It defines what kinds of nodes and edges can exist and what they mean. The knowledge graph is the data: actual customers, actual invoices, actual links.[Neo4j’s explanation](https://neo4j.com/blog/knowledge-graph/taxonomy-vs-ontology-vs-knowledge-graph/) puts it well: the knowledge graph is what you build, while taxonomies and ontologies are the blueprints.


[IBM defines a knowledge graph](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/knowledge-graph) as a network of real-world entities and their relationships, made of nodes, edges, and labels, and notes that ontologies provide its formal structure. Knowledge graphs earn their keep on multi-hop questions and on unstructured text. Microsoft’s[GraphRAG research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130) , for example, showed that an LLM-built entity graph beats plain vector retrieval on “global” questions over large document collections.


## Ontology vs Semantic Layer


The simplest distinction is **meaning vs measurement** . An ontology defines what things are and how they relate. A[semantic layer](https://upsolve.ai/blog/semantic-layer-ai) defines how to compute numbers about them. They overlap on entities and joins, which is why the terms get blurred.


The overlap has a useful edge case. In[dbt Labs’ 2026 benchmark](https://docs.getdbt.com/blog/semantic-layer-vs-text-to-sql-2026) , the[dbt Semantic Layer](https://upsolve.ai/blog/dbt-semantic-layer) answered 100% of in-scope questions, but the remaining misses were questions that needed “too many entity hops for MetricFlow.” Traversing many relationships is precisely what ontologies and knowledge graphs are built for. A[metrics layer](https://upsolve.ai/blog/metrics-layer) handles the number; an ontology handles the path to it.


One more caution: in knowledge management circles, “semantic layer” sometimes means the opposite.[Enterprise Knowledge](https://enterprise-knowledge.com/what-is-the-difference-between-a-semantic-layer-and-a-context-layer/) describes a semantic layer *built on* taxonomies, ontologies, and knowledge graphs. If two people disagree about which contains which, they’re probably from different fields.


## What Is Palantir’s Ontology?


The Palantir Ontology is the layer inside Palantir Foundry that maps an organization’s data and models to real-world objects, their relationships, and the actions people (and AI agents) can take on them. Palantir’s docs call it[“an operational layer for the organization”](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/ontology/overview/) that in many settings “serves as a digital twin of the organization.”


### Objects, Properties, and Links (the Semantic Half)


-


**Object type:**[“the schema definition of a real-world entity or event”](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/object-types-overview/) , such as` Employee` or` Flight` . Each object is one instance, such as a specific employee.


-


**Property:** a characteristic of an object type, like a flight’s departure time. Properties can serve as primary keys.


-


**Link type:**[“the schema definition of a relationship between two object types”](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/object-link-types/link-types-overview/) , such as Flight → Aircraft or Employee → Manager.


-


**Interface:** a shared shape that several object types implement. For example,` Airport` and` Manufacturing Plant` both implement a` Facility` interface.


### Actions and Functions (the Kinetic Half)


This is what makes Palantir different from a catalog. **Action types** are[“the definition of a set of changes or edits to objects, property values, and links”](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/action-types/overview/) , and edits can be written back to operational systems. **Functions** let developers write business logic in TypeScript or Python that reads properties, traverses links, and makes edits. Palantir describes the full Ontology as semantic elements (objects, properties, links) plus kinetic elements (actions, functions, dynamic security).


### Ontology vs Foundry vs AIP


-


**Foundry** is the data platform.


-


**The Ontology** is the layer within Foundry that turns datasets into objects, links, and actions.


-


**AIP** is Palantir’s AI tooling built on top of the Ontology.[AIP Logic](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/logic/overview/) , for example, is a no-code environment for LLM-powered functions that take Ontology objects as input and can edit them.


-


**The Ontology SDK (OSDK)** gives developers typed access to the Ontology from TypeScript, Python, and Java.


### Why Palantir Says It’s “Not a Semantic Layer”


Palantir argues that a thin semantic layer can’t capture how an enterprise actually works. Its Ontology integrates data, logic, action, and security, and it is[“designed to represent the complex, interconnected decisions of an enterprise, not simply the data.”](https://www.palantir.com/docs/foundry/architecture-center/ontology-system/) In Palantir’s framing, semantics must be paired with kinetics.


## Ontology in AI: Why Agents Suddenly Need One


LLMs are good at language and bad at guessing your business. An ontology gives them the missing structure, and the evidence is consistent:


-


**data.world (2023):** GPT-4 answered 16.7% of insurance questions correctly from SQL and 54.2% from an ontology-backed knowledge graph. On high-complexity schemas, SQL scored **0%** and the knowledge graph scored 35.7–38.5%.


-


**data.world follow-up (2024):** Adding[ontology-based query checks and LLM repair](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11706) raised accuracy to 72%, with another 8% answered “I don’t know” instead of guessing wrong.


-


**An independent 2026 ablation** on the DABStep benchmark found that[semantic content drove most of the gain](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22259) , lifting hard-task accuracy from 13.9–37.0% to 55.1–77.4% across four models. Agent scaffolding alone added 0–15 points. Governed agents also issued zero data-modifying statements, compared with 166 for ungoverned ones.


-


**Databricks** reports that Genie with Ontology answered 84.5% of 28 enterprise questions correctly on the first attempt, compared with 52.4% for the strongest general-purpose coding agent tested. Databricks itself calls this an internal benchmark.


> **The pattern:** model scaffolding helps a little. Encoded business meaning helps a lot.


### The 2025–2026 Ontology Wave


-


**Microsoft Fabric IQ** (announced November 2025) includes an[ontology item](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/iq/ontology/overview) with entity types, relationships, rules, and actions, bootstrapped from existing Power BI semantic models. It imports and exports OWL and RDF. As of October 2026 it is still in preview.


-


**Databricks Genie Ontology** (June 2026) is described as[“a new self-improving context layer”](https://www.databricks.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/databricks-launches-genie-one-all-new-agentic-coworker-every-team) that extracts business knowledge from tools like Slack, Jira, and Confluence. It builds on[Databricks metric views](https://upsolve.ai/blog/databricks-semantic-layer) in Unity Catalog.


-


**Snowflake** doesn’t use the word. Its equivalent,[Horizon Context](https://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/horizon-context-governed-context/) , is branded a governed context layer. Its semantic piece is[Snowflake semantic views](https://upsolve.ai/blog/snowflake-semantic-layer) .


### Formal vs Operational Ontologies


This is the distinction that resolves most of the confusion. A **formal ontology** (OWL, RDF) is built for logical reasoning and interoperability between systems. An **operational ontology** (Palantir, Fabric IQ, Genie, Upsolve Data Models) binds business objects to live data, permissions, and sometimes actions, so software and agents can use them. Analytics teams almost always need the second kind. It’s also why vendors increasingly use ontology and[context layer](https://upsolve.ai/blog/context-layer) interchangeably.


## How to Build a Data Ontology for an Analytics Agent


You don’t need a PhD in OWL or a triple store to give an analytics agent an ontology. You need the operational minimum:


1.


**Model the head first.** List the 10–20 entities your most common questions touch: customers, accounts, subscriptions, invoices, products.


2.


**Describe tables and columns in business language.** Include units, exclusions, and which table is the source of truth. A good[data dictionary](https://upsolve.ai/blog/data-dictionary) is the starting point.


3.


**Declare keys and relationships.** Primary and foreign keys are your ontology’s links.


4.


**Write canonical definitions** for the metrics people argue about, such as ARR, active customer, and churn.


5.


**Capture allowed values and permissions.** Statuses, plan tiers, and regions, plus who can see what, enforced outside the model.


Then version it, test it against real questions, and add a definition every time an agent gets something wrong.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is data ontology in simple terms?


A data ontology is an agreed map of the things your business cares about and how they connect. It defines what a customer, an order, or an invoice is, what attributes each has, and the rules that apply, so every system and person interprets the data the same way.


### What is an example of an ontology?


A simple business example: a Customer holds one or more Subscriptions, each Subscription is on one Plan and generates Invoices, and an Overdue Invoice is an open invoice past its due date. Well-known published ontologies include the Gene Ontology, SNOMED CT for clinical terms, FIBO for finance, and[Schema.org](http://schema.org/) .


### Is a knowledge graph the same as an ontology?


No. An ontology is the schema: the types of things and relationships that can exist. A knowledge graph is that schema populated with real data. Put simply, ontology plus data equals knowledge graph.


### What is the difference between an ontology and a semantic layer?


An ontology defines meaning: entities, relationships, and rules. A semantic layer defines measurement: how metrics compile to SQL. They overlap on entities and joins, but the semantic layer is built for consistent numbers and the ontology for consistent understanding.


### What is an ontology in AI?


In AI, an ontology is structured business knowledge an agent can use to interpret questions and data correctly. Grounding LLMs in an ontology or knowledge graph has tripled question-answering accuracy in published benchmarks, mainly by removing guesswork about what terms mean and how tables connect.


### What are the types of ontology?


Ontologies are commonly grouped into four types: upper ontologies (very general concepts like time and space), domain ontologies (one field, such as medicine or finance), task ontologies (a specific activity), and application ontologies (one system or use case). Most business ontologies are domain or application ontologies.
